title: NtM · works in the channel
noticeText:
Example only. The working group also wants this picture to carry Forth Ports Notices to Mariners — not as a separate PDF a skipper may never open, but as a pin on the same chart FTNS already sends for a berth.

A typical notice of this kind: dredging, survey, or temporary reduction of navigable width. Leisure users and small harbours hear about it late, or not at all. Putting the live notice here means a visiting yacht looking for Granton also sees the warning on the way in.

Live notices stay official Forth Ports /  FTNS text. This pin is the shape of the layer, not a substitute for the published NtM.
aim: Show the notice on the water it affects

title: NtM · works at Leith
noticeText:
Example only. Port works, dive operations or a temporary exclusion at Leith are issued as Notices to Mariners. A leisure skipper still often finds out from a club WhatsApp.

The proposal is that the same guide used for visitor berths shows the current Forth notices on the place they apply. Granton and Port Edgar sit close enough that a Leith notice is not only a commercial-port problem.
affects: Approaches and visitors near Leith / Granton

title: NtM · bridges / Queensferry
noticeText:
Example only. Temporary exclusions, bridge works or a large cruise at anchor under the Forth Bridges are exactly the notices Port Edgar and a visiting yacht need on the same picture as the visitor-berth card.

FTNS already issues the notice. The working group is asking that the notice also live here, next to the berth and the race weekend, so one link answers the radio call.
whyhere: Cruise, works and racing already share this water
